text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) and Alliance For Democracy (Aford) central committees on Monday endorsed a proposal to merge and agreed that a joint committee should consider the name and party symbols, a senior Aford official said.
- A woman was killed and nine seriously hurt in a collision between a minibus taxi and bus in Blantyre.
- Former presidential aide Kalonga Stambuli is expected to appear in court accused of misallocating funds for President Bakili Muluzi's International Appeal Fund for Clean Water.
- The national executives of the MCP and Aford n Monday resolved all outstanding issues on their intended merger and agreed to open the door to any other party holding similar views.

- A hearing of the Press Trust judicial review was adjourned on Monday to allow further action by MCP lawyers who are contesting the takeover by the government of former president Kamuzu Banda's Press Corporation.
